expected_effect: Full 1800 s run: steps >= 2250 (predicted ~2350 from additive per-step timing: 0.869 - (0.869-0.767) ... i.e. ~0.765 s/step) and public val_bpb <= 1.0000, i.e. at least 0.0057 below the pinned control 1.005734 and below the --bf16-sdpa-input KEEP (1.002028). Falsified (DISCARD) if val_bpb >= 1.005734 with steps >= 2200, which would mean the non-MLP BF16 norm sites themselves degrade quality. CONFOUNDED if steps < 2200.
hypothesis: The two bracketing runs at 9a4caa7b decompose the --bf16-norm-output result: BF16 at ONLY the MLP-input norm gave +13% steps (2346 vs 2071) but +0.014 BPB (1.020187 / 1.019731 vs 1.005734), while BF16 at ALL norm sites gave +31% steps (2716) and 1.016279 -- i.e. adding the non-MLP sites (q/k/v norms, local-conv norm, final norm) on top of the MLP site added ~370 steps and LOWERED BPB by 0.0035. Together with the --bf16-sdpa-input KEEP (attention-side BF16, 2233 steps, 1.002028), this says the quality damage of the full policy is localized to the MLP-input boundary, whereas the attention/final-norm BF16 boundaries are quality-neutral speedups. Therefore the complement policy -- BF16 norm outputs at every norm site EXCEPT the norm whose result enters self.mlp -- should retain roughly half of the full policy's step gain (~0.10 s/step: control 0.869 s/step, mlp-only 0.767, full 0.663; predicted ~0.765 s/step => ~2350 steps) with no quality penalty, and thus lower val_bpb below the control.

single_causal_change: One numerical-format policy change confined to train.py: a new module-level toggle USE_BF16_NORM_OUTPUT_EXCEPT_MLP (default True; env NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_BF16_NORM_OUTPUT_EXCEPT_MLP='0' disables; CLI --bf16-norm-output-except-mlp/--no-bf16-norm-output-except-mlp; appended to ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES so checkpoints persist it and load_for_eval restores it). When True it (i) makes the existing norm-output policy constant USE_BF16_NORM_OUTPUT effective (exactly the state produced by passing --bf16-norm-output, so every code path that reads that constant behaves exactly as in the already-run al-20260922-bf16-norm-output-policy-r3-full-r1 arm) and (ii) exempts exactly the norm() call(s) in Block.forward whose result is the direct input of self.mlp(...): those calls execute the control's non-cast path and return the input dtype (FP32 in the default serial path). Relative to the already-run --bf16-norm-output arm the only difference is the dtype of the MLP-input norm output; relative to the already-run mlp-input-norm-only arm it is the exact complement site set. No optimizer, schedule, kernel, data, evaluator, or shape change; with the toggle off the program is behavior-identical to 9a4caa7b defaults.
